subject: ClearVault networking impact summary & action requests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Patel <sofia@clearvault.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearVault networking impact summary & action requests

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the call this morning. Recap and open asks below so we have a single source of truth as we decide between Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC.

Summary (what we heard)
- Preferred hosting: your team is leaning toward Private VPC (AWS) for data isolation and egress control.
- Primary technical concerns: PrivateLink vs VPC peering, static egress IPs for third-party allowlists, and SOC2 evidence for audit.
- Timeline: you mentioned a POC target in mid-November.

Open technical/action items for ClearVault (please confirm owners and dates)
1) Confirm which connectivity pattern you prefer: PrivateLink (recommended for minimal routing changes) or VPC peering (if you need direct VPC-level routing). owner: ClearVault NetOps (netops@clearvault.com) — due: 2026-11-10
2) Confirm whether you manage outbound NAT and egress IPs or prefer Redwood-managed NAT (we can provide a fixed egress block for PrivateLink). owner: ClearVault NetOps — due: 2026-11-10
3) Provide target CIDR(s) to allowlist for inbound control plane/management if you want a restricted management plane. owner: ClearVault NetOps — due: 2026-11-10
4) Security questionnaire and SOC2 log retention questions — attach security doc and let us know a point of contact. owner: ClearVault Security — due: 2026-11-12

What Redwood will do next
- Ben and Jasmine will draft an egress IP list and a short network checklist for PrivateLink integration.
- We’ll prepare a short comparison doc (latency/maintainability) for PrivateLink vs peering for your architecture.
- Schedule a 60-min NetOps deep-dive (we suggested 2026-11-12 or 11-13).

Attachments: clearvault_postcall_slides.pdf (post-call slides), network_readiness_checklist.csv (template)

Please reply with the preferred connectivity option and NetOps contact if different from netops@clearvault.com. If you want Redwood to prepare a draft allowlist immediately, say so and we’ll push the egress CSV.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Marissa — thanks for the recap and clear asks. Quick responses below: 

- Connectivity: ClearVault NetOps prefers PrivateLink (we want endpoint-level controls and to avoid cross-VPC routing complexity).
- Egress: we will manage outbound NAT for our workloads; however, our security team requires a fixed set of Redwood egress IPs to add to our external allowlists (third-party APIs).
- Management plane: prefer locking to specific management IPs if Redwood can provide them; otherwise we’ll create a CIDR to allowlist.
- Security POC contact: me (Sofia) for coordination and Claire from Security (claire@clearvault.com) for questionnaire items.

We attached our security_requirements.docx — Claire will review details. POC week of 2026-11-16 works. Please include NetOps in the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Sofia Patel
Head of Product, ClearVault
sofia@clearvault.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Patel <sofia@clearvault.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 13:05:10 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearVault networking impact summary & action requests

Thanks — quick technical notes from NetOps side.

PrivateLink (AWS) notes:
- Redwood exposes an AWS NLB-backed endpoint service in our account. Customer creates an Interface VPC Endpoint in their VPC that connects to our service. This keeps traffic on the AWS network and avoids peering route management.
- For PrivateLink we still terminate TLS at Redwood; mutual TLS is possible if you require client certs — we support mTLS on the endpoint with an additional config and cert exchange.
- Egress behavior: with PrivateLink, outbound to third parties (internet) originates from Redwood egress if the call crosses our backend; if you want all third-party calls to originate from your NAT, we can ship a variant that uses an egress proxy through your VPC. We need to know which pattern for the POC.

Required info from ClearVault to produce a final allowlist/plan:
1) VPC ID and region (e.g., vpc-abc123, us-west-2)
2) Desired management-plane CIDR or static IP(s) for control-plane allowlist
3) If using mTLS: contact to exchange certs (or we can use token-based TLS).

Proposed next deliverable: Redwood will produce an egress ip file and a short mapping doc describing inbound ports (443) and recommended security groups. I attached redwood_egress_ips_v1.csv (draft) to save you time.

Ben Carter
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Sofia Patel <sofia@clearvault.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Torres <claire@clearvault.com>, Network Ops <netops@clearvault.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 08:18:35 -0500
Subject: Re: ClearVault networking impact summary & action requests

Ben — that all makes sense. A few clarifications from netops/security after a quick internal sync: 
- PrivateLink is our path of choice.
- For third-party allowlists we will need a fixed egress block from Redwood OR we will route third-party traffic via our NAT. For the POC, routing via our NAT is preferred so we can validate observability.
- Management-plane IPs: please propose the smallest possible CIDR for management; we prefer a /28 if feasible.
- SOC2/logs: Claire asked whether Redwood can publish access logs to a customer S3 or provide a consolidated archive for SOC2 review. Please advise.

POC scheduling: week of 2026-11-16 still good. NetOps can do 2026-11-17 10:00–11:00 PT. Can you send a calendar invite?

Attachments: clearvault_security_requirements.docx

Sofia
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Thanks all — quick follow-up with proposed next steps and owners: 

1) NetOps deep-dive (60m) — proposed: 2026-11-17 10:00 PT. Marissa will send the invite. owner: Marissa / Ben.
2) Redwood to deliver final egress list adjusted for your decision to route third-party traffic via ClearVault NAT (we’ll mark which flows originate from your NAT vs ours). deliverable due: 2026-11-12. owner: Ben.
3) Management-plane CIDR proposal — Redwood to propose a /28 for restricted control-plane access; we’ll include required ports and protocol details in the doc. deliverable due: 2026-11-10. owner: Ben.
4) SOC2 access logs options — Jasmine will coordinate with Security to confirm whether we can push logs to a customer S3 or supply a signed archive; expected answer by 2026-11-12. owner: Jasmine.
5) Mutual action plan + kickoff agenda — draft link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/MA-PLA-N-12345 (internal > ClearVault share). owner: Marissa.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx
